name: OkunNLP: English-Okun Parallel Corpus
description: OkunNLP is the first English-Okun parallel corpus, comprising 5,015 verse-aligned sentence pairs extracted from six books of the Okun Bible (Bible Society of Nigeria, 2022) and aligned with the public-domain King James Version. The corpus supports neural machine translation research for Okun, a Northeast Yoruba dialect cluster spoken by over two million people in Kogi State, Nigeria.

spatialCoverage.name: Kogi State, Nigeria
spatialCoverage.description: Okun-speaking regions including Ijumu, Yagba West, Yagba East, Kabba/Bunu, and Mopa-Muro Local Government Areas

distribution.name: okun_corpus_final.csv
distribution.description: Complete parallel corpus in CSV format with UTF-8 encoding. Contains columns: Reference, English (KJV), Okun, OCR_Confidence, Split.

distribution.name: data_splits
distribution.description: Train/development/test splits (80/10/10) contained within the main corpus CSV via the Split column

recordSet.name: parallel_sentences
recordSet.description: English-Okun parallel sentence pairs aligned at verse level. Total: 5,015 pairs from six biblical books (Psalms, Job, Proverbs, Ecclesiastes, Song of Solomon, Isaiah 1-10). Quality-filtered experimental subset: 1,959 pairs (train=1,567, dev=196, test=196).

field.name: Reference
field.description: Biblical verse reference in format 'Book Chapter:Verse' (e.g., 'Psalms 1:1', 'Job 1:1'). Serves as unique identifier for each sentence pair.

field.name: English (KJV)
field.description: English sentence from the King James Version Bible (public domain). Source language for machine translation tasks.

field.name: Okun
field.description: Okun translation from the Okun Bible (Bible Society of Nigeria, 2022). Contains diacritical marks including subdot vowels and tone marks. Target language for machine translation tasks. Encoding: UTF-8.

field.name: OCR_Confidence
field.description: Google Cloud Vision API confidence score for the OCR extraction (0.0-1.0). Used for quality filtering; experimental subset uses threshold > 0.85.

field.name: Split
field.description: Dataset split assignment: 'train', 'dev', or 'test'. Only present for the 1,959 quality-filtered pairs; remaining 3,056 pairs have value 'full_only'.

rai:dataCollection: The corpus was constructed via dual-column OCR extraction from the printed Okun Bible (Bible Society of Nigeria, 2022). Collection involved: (1) Smartphone photography of six biblical books in landscape orientation. (2) Page splitting: PDF pages rendered at 300 DPI, rotated 270 degrees, split vertically at midpoint. (3) Image enhancement: contrast x1.3, sharpness x1.5. (4) OCR via Google Cloud Vision API (Tesseract discarded due to diacritic failure). (5) Verse alignment using deterministic counters from known chapter-verse counts. Discrepancies flagged for manual review; incomplete verses marked [MISSING]. No content-based exclusions; all exclusions due to OCR quality. Manual quality review by native Okun speakers (Ijumu dialect) on 100 randomly selected pairs showed 91% alignment accuracy, 83% diacritic preservation, 89% text integrity. Collection timeframe: October 2024 - April 2026.
rai:dataBiases: Domain bias: Corpus restricted to six biblical books, skewing toward theological/literary register and excluding modern conversational, technical, news, commercial, and administrative vocabulary. Genre bias: High formulaic repetition in wisdom literature (Proverbs) and poetry (Psalms) reduces lexical/syntactic diversity; models may memorize patterns rather than learn generalizable translation. Dialect bias: Okun Bible translated from Yoruba Common Language Bible, potentially introducing Yoruba lexical influence (e.g., 'awon' substituting Okun 'oghon' for third-person plural). OCR quality bias: Confidence scores range 0.42-0.98 (mean 0.81); Psalms chapters 100-150 show 38% diacritic omission due to spine curvature. Language proxy bias: Models fine-tuned with Yoruba (yor_Latn) as proxy since no Okun code exists, causing systematic Yoruba lexical bleed and subdot vowel omission. Geographic bias: Quality review used only Ijumu dialect speakers; seven Okun sub-varieties (Bunu, Ijumu, Owe, Oworo, Iyagba, Ikiri, Gbede) may vary.
rai:personalSensitiveInformation: The corpus contains no personal information, sensitive data, or identifiable information. All content is biblical text (Okun Bible and King James Version). No references to living individuals. containsPII=false. No privacy preservation methods required.
rai:dataUseCases: Intended uses: Training and evaluating neural machine translation models for English-Okun and Okun-English translation; establishing baseline MT benchmarks for Okun; fine-tuning multilingual pre-trained models (M2M100, NLLB-200, mBART); studying transfer learning for low-resource African languages; corpus linguistics research on Okun morphology and syntax; educational resources for Okun language preservation. Out-of-scope uses: General-purpose Okun translation beyond biblical domain (out-of-domain BLEU drops 48-49 points); real-time production systems without additional training; commercial services (license is CC-BY-NC-4.0); Southwest/Southeast Yoruba dialect models; medical/legal/safety-critical translation without human oversight.
rai:dataLimitations: Small corpus size (5,015 pairs) limits model capacity. Restricted to religious biblical domain with no conversational or technical text. OCR-induced diacritical errors in approximately 17% of verses, concentrated in low-confidence extractions (confidence < 0.70 shows 38% diacritic omission). Text-only corpus cannot directly support ASR/TTS. Yoruba language proxy introduces systematic lexical biases. Test set is strictly in-domain from same six books as training data; out-of-domain evaluation shows 48-49 BLEU point drops (Genesis narrative test). No dialectal annotation distinguishing seven Okun sub-varieties. English source uses 1611 King James Version with archaic vocabulary. No linguistic annotations beyond sentence alignment.
